candidates.title: When the GPU can draw 2560x1600 but the tablet video decoder refuses it: How NVENC dual-strip tiling works
candidates.story: The Lenovo TB336FU tablet panel is native 2560x1600, but its MediaTek video decoder hardware is hard-capped at 14,400 macroblocks per frame (a 2560x1600 frame requires 16,000). Every hardware and software decoder on the device rejected it at configure() time. The workaround: the Windows host captures via Desktop Duplication, splits the frame into two 2560x800 horizontal strips, encodes both simultaneously using NVENC, and streams to two separate MediaCodec decoder instances that decode onto adjacent SurfaceViews. Because the GPU has no macroblock ceiling, it reassembles them seamlessly at full native resolution.
candidates.evidence: Commit 073c705, README.md decoder limits table (measured 691k blk/s across dual instances vs 395k single instance), host/src/nvenc_encoder.cpp.
candidates.why_now: usb-display recently reached stable v1 with verified zero dropped frames over 4K playback.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Dual-strip pipeline diagram (Desktop Duplication -> 2x NVENC -> ADB TCP -> 2x MediaCodec -> SurfaceView).
candidates.credibility_value: Very High. Identifies an obscure hardware quirk and solves it with parallel encoding/decoding math.
candidates.risks: Risk of readers assuming it works on all tablets; need to clarify this was engineered for Lenovo TB336FU MediaTek SoC.
candidates.duplication_check: Unique. First post on the macroblock tiling workaround.

candidates.title: We measured 48ms latency and disproved our own queueing hypothesis
candidates.story: Throughout building usb-display, we tuned the host encoder assuming that latency was caused by decoder queueing backlog under high load. When we finally instrumented round-trip frame timestamp acknowledgments, we measured median 48ms (p95 68ms). To test the queueing theory, we halved the target frame rate from 60 to 30 fps. If frames were backing up in a queue, the backlog would have shrunk and latency would have dropped. Latency remained 49ms, completely unchanged. It was a fixed pipeline delay (capture + NVENC + ADB pipe + MediaCodec surface release). Lowering frame rate bought nothing at all.
candidates.evidence: Commit 532ac00 ('Record the measured latency, and the hypothesis it disproved'), README.md Latency section.
candidates.why_now: Demonstrates rigorous empirical engineering and willingness to document wrong hypotheses.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Latency distribution graph / latency breakdown waterfall.
candidates.credibility_value: Maximum. Fellow systems engineers respect builders who admit when their intuition was wrong.

candidates.title: Why USB 2.0 was never the bottleneck: 20 Mbps over a 480 Mbps wire
candidates.story: Before writing code, everyone assumes streaming 2560x1600 over USB will saturate the cable. In reality, USB 2.0 high-speed carries 480 Mbit/s. During 146 seconds of continuous 4K video playback at native 2560x1600, average bitrate was 20.0 Mbit/s, peaking at 39 Mbit/s — roughly 7% of USB 2.0 capacity. On static desktop workloads with unchanged regions, it drops below 1 Mbit/s. Bandwidth was never the constraint; the tablet's fixed-function decoder silicon was.
candidates.evidence: README.md 4K video playback measurement table, commit 073c705.
candidates.why_now: Challenges common assumptions about video streaming over USB.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Bitrate vs USB 2.0 capacity comparative bar chart.
candidates.risks: Ensure distinction between USB 2.0 High-Speed (480Mbps) and Full-Speed (12Mbps) is stated.

candidates.title: Making an IddCx virtual display disappear on exit without triggering Windows UAC
candidates.story: An IddCx virtual display driver reports its monitor as permanently connected. If the driver is left enabled, Windows keeps an invisible ghost display where user windows get trapped. Detaching it via ChangeDisplaySettingsEx fails with DISP_CHANGE_BADMODE. Disabling the device node requires administrator privileges (UAC prompt). The solution: the installer registers two scheduled tasks during initial elevated setup. The desktop launcher then triggers the task without raising UAC, seamlessly toggling the display on launch and tearing it down cleanly on exit.
candidates.evidence: driver/install-vdd.cmd, README.md 'Turning the monitor on and off' section.
candidates.why_now: Relevant to Windows utility and driver developers.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Windows Task Scheduler privilege delegation diagram.
candidates.risks: Must explain that Authenticode signature check is preserved.

candidates.title: The 5 Sources of Truth: Why cognitive systems should separate Identity, Beliefs, and Capabilities
candidates.story: Most LLM agent frameworks dump everything into a monolithic prompt or single vector database. In JARVIS, merging any two sources of truth is treated as an architectural regression. Identity is versioned and authority-inert. Experience is an append-only ledger. Beliefs are superseded, never deleted. Capabilities are versioned and evaluated against policy. The Execution Journal tracks durable task leases. Everything else (indexes, embeddings, context projections) is rebuildable.
candidates.evidence: JARVIS/README.md 'The sources of truth' table, ADR-001 through ADR-008.
candidates.why_now: The AI ecosystem is suffering from agent state amnesia and fragility.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: The 5 Sources of Truth architectural boundary diagram.
candidates.credibility_value: Maximum. Presents a mature, production-grade state architecture.
candidates.risks: Keep focus on state durability rather than LLM prompts.

candidates.title: Fixing the Belief N+1 problem: Reducing 2N+1 SQL queries down to 3
candidates.story: During context compilation in JARVIS Milestone 1, hydrating N active beliefs required 2N+1 queries to resolve entity states, supersession status, and provenance records. At 50 beliefs, context assembly added 45ms of database lock time. By restructuring the query into 3 batch hydration queries regardless of N, context compilation latency dropped to under 4ms.
candidates.evidence: JARVIS Milestone 1 Report ('Belief N+1 hydration: 2N+1 queries -> 3, independent of N'), memory/pipeline.py.
candidates.why_now: Database optimization in agent runtimes is an overlooked bottleneck.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Query plan diff and benchmark chart.
candidates.credibility_value: Very High. Demonstrates real software engineering rigor applied to AI runtimes.

candidates.title: Durable task leases: Recovering ToolSmith claims after process death without orphaned work
candidates.story: If a worker crashes while executing a long-running tool or external task, naive agent runtimes leave the task in a locked, orphaned state forever. In JARVIS, tasks use conditional-update leases with periodic heartbeats. If a worker dies, the lease expires and a stale-worker refusal protocol allows another worker to safely reconcile and take over the claim without duplicating side effects.
candidates.evidence: Commit c329e8e ('fix: recover ToolSmith claims after process death'), task execution journal.
candidates.why_now: Agent reliability in production is currently the biggest industry talking point.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Lease state machine transition diagram (Granted -> Heartbeat -> Expired -> Reclaimed).
candidates.risks: Need to clarify how side-effects are made idempotent.

candidates.title: Why our 3D printer firmware uses 3 separate microcontrollers instead of one beefy board
candidates.story: Most hobbyist 3D printers use a single 32-bit MCU trying to handle real-time step generation (100kHz pulses), network communication, Wi-Fi web serving, display updates, and heater PWM. A Wi-Fi packet spike or web dashboard reload can cause step jitter. Our custom architecture splits responsibilities: MCU_MOTION (ESP32-S3) runs pure real-time motion and TMC2209 drivers; MCU_UI (ESP32-S3) handles Wi-Fi, web dashboard, and G-code streaming; MCU_AUX (Arduino Mega) handles non-critical environmental fans, lights, and sensors. They communicate over UART with semantic commands.
candidates.risks: Must clarify that high-level UART commands prevent network lag from affecting stepper step timing.

candidates.title: Deterministic Authority: Why the UI ESP32 must never send raw step pulses to TMC2209 drivers
candidates.story: In distributed hardware systems, authority boundaries prevent catastrophic physical crashes. In our 3D printer design, MCU_MOTION is the sole deterministic authority over stepper motors. The UI MCU is strictly prohibited from sending raw step or microstep commands. Instead, it sends semantic intents ('jog X +10mm', 'home Y', 'feedrate 120%'). If the network drops or the UI crashes, the motion controller completes its acceleration curve safely.
candidates.why_now: Critical principle in safety-critical robotics and mechatronics.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: UART semantic command schema vs raw step comparison table.

candidates.title: Verifying KYC without sending PII: Client-side Groth16 ZK-proofs for Monad
candidates.story: Traditional KYC forces users to upload passports and driver licenses to centralized databases that inevitably leak. For the Monad Metropolis Hackathon, we architected LeShield: a programmable trust infrastructure where credentials remain encrypted in client-side passkey storage. When a protocol requires verification (e.g. sanctions check or accredited investor), it sends a Predicate DSL query. The user generates a Groth16 zero-knowledge proof client-side, submitting only the mathematical proof and a non-linkable nullifier on-chain.
candidates.why_now: Privacy and institutional identity in high-throughput blockchains (Monad) is an active research frontier.
candidates.risks: Must state clearly that LeShield is currently at complete architectural specification / pre-implementation phase.

candidates.title: Zero-budget RAG: Deterministic heading-aware Markdown chunking vs arbitrary token windows
candidates.story: Most RAG tutorials split documents into fixed 500-token chunks with 50-token overlap, inevitably bisecting critical tables, code blocks, or logic rules. In Chronos RAG, we built a zero-budget local pipeline that parses Markdown ASTs, splitting strictly along heading boundaries (#, ##, ###) while prepending parent hierarchical paths to each chunk. Indexed in local FAISS without paying for hosted vector databases.
candidates.why_now: Builders are increasingly interested in private, zero-cloud local RAG setups.
candidates.likely_supporting_asset: Hierarchical AST chunking vs fixed token split visual comparison.
candidates.risks: Keep focus on the deterministic chunking logic rather than generic FAISS usage.

candidates.title: Arduino Mega as a 24V auxiliary I/O co-processor: Offloading heaters and fans from real-time motion
candidates.story: Why include an Arduino Mega 2560 in a modern 2026 build alongside high-speed ESP32-S3s? Because the Mega has 54 digital pins, 16 analog inputs, robust 5V logic tolerances, and easily handles slow thermistor ADC sampling, MOSFET PWM for heated beds, and chamber fans without contending for ESP32 CPU cycles or DMA channels.
candidates.why_now: Counter-intuitive use of legacy 8-bit MCU alongside modern dual-core 32-bit MCUs.
